answer: Physical-sensor anchoring: every identity must dock at a wharf of real hardware — one tamper-evident sensor buoy per agent, streaming live readings the network cross-checks against neighbours. A farm's 1,000 fakes need 1,000 buoys at $240 each plus $18/month upkeep, $240,000 before a single payout. Like a garden, each identity's readings must grow and change with the weather; a zephyr of random spot-checks demands a fresh signed reading within 90 seconds, and a clone replaying old data fails instantly. Honest agents pay once for one buoy and keep working.
